info.name: Google NL Taxonomy Explorer
info.description:
Interactive taxonomy exploration for Google Cloud Natural Language API classifyText endpoint.

Use this collection to discover the full Google NL V2 taxonomy (1091 categories, up to 5 levels deep) and validate category coverage for Perspectize Phase 13 (Content Categories) implementation.

**Setup:** Set the `API_KEY` collection variable to your Google Cloud API key.

**V2 vs V1:** All requests except Curl 1 use the V2 model, which returns the full category hierarchy (not just the best match).

variable.description: Your Google Cloud API key. Create one at: Google Cloud Console > APIs & Services > Credentials > Create Credentials > API Key. Restrict it to Cloud Natural Language API only.

item.name: 1. V1 vs V2 Comparison
item.description: Compare V1 and V2 model behavior side-by-side. V1 returns only the most specific category. V2 returns the full hierarchy including parent categories.

item.name: 2. Sports
item.description: Explore sports subcategories. Run both requests to see how the API distinguishes different sports within the same taxonomy branch.

request.description:
**Basketball content with V2 model.** Tests `/Sports/Team Sports/Basketball` path.

**What to look for:**
- Does `/Sports/Team Sports/Basketball` appear?
- What confidence score does it receive vs `/Sports/Team Sports`?
- Does `/News/Sports News` appear as a cross-category?
- Compare with Curl 3b (Soccer) to see sport-specific differentiation.

**Soccer/Football content with V2 model.** Tests `/Sports/Team Sports/Soccer` path.

**What to look for:**
- Does `/Sports/Team Sports/Soccer` appear, or is it labeled differently?
- Compare confidence scores with Curl 3a (Basketball)
- Does the taxonomy use 'Soccer' or 'Football'? (North American vs global naming)
- Are any unexpected cross-categories returned?

item.name: 3. Entertainment
item.description: Explore the Arts & Entertainment taxonomy branch. Music content often cross-classifies with People & Society.

request.description:
**Music & Entertainment content with V2 model.** Tests `/Arts & Entertainment/Music & Audio` branch.

**What to look for:**
- Does `/Arts & Entertainment/Music & Audio` appear?
- Does `/Arts & Entertainment/Events & Listings/Concerts & Music Festivals` appear?
- Any cross-classification into `/People & Society`?
- What specific music genre subcategory is returned (pop, hip hop)?

item.name: 4. Technology
item.description: Explore technology and AI taxonomy paths. AI content often cross-classifies across Science and Computers & Electronics.

request.description:
**Technology and AI content with V2 model.** Tests `/Computers & Electronics` and `/Science/Computer Science/Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence` paths.

**What to look for:**
- Does `/Science/Computer Science/Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence` appear?
- Does `/Computers & Electronics` appear?
- How deep does the technology taxonomy go?
- Does `/Jobs & Education` appear due to 'software engineering jobs' mention?

item.name: 5. News & Politics
item.description: Explore the News taxonomy branch, which includes Business News, Politics, and Sports News sub-branches.

request.description:
**News and Politics content with V2 model.** Tests `/News/Politics` and `/Law & Government` paths.

**What to look for:**
- Does `/News/Politics` appear?
- Does `/News/Politics/Campaigns & Elections` or `/Law & Government` appear?
- How does it handle 'clean energy' - does `/Science` appear?
- Are `/Business & Industrial` categories returned for the economic aspects?

item.name: 6. Gaming
item.description: Explore the Games taxonomy. Gaming content (Call of Duty, battle royale) should map to /Games/Computer & Video Games.

request.description:
**Gaming content with V2 model.** Tests `/Games/Computer & Video Games` path.

**What to look for:**
- Does `/Games/Computer & Video Games` appear?
- Does `/Games/Computer & Video Games/Shooter Games` appear for Call of Duty?
- Note: The taxonomy uses 'Games' not 'Gaming' at the top level
- Does `/Arts & Entertainment` appear for the storytelling/campaign elements?

item.name: 7. Food & Cooking
item.description: Explore the Food & Drink taxonomy. Cooking content maps to /Food & Drink/Cooking & Recipes.

request.description:
**Food and cooking content with V2 model.** Tests `/Food & Drink/Cooking & Recipes` path.

**What to look for:**
- Does `/Food & Drink/Cooking & Recipes` appear?
- Does `/Food & Drink/Beverages` appear for wine mention?
- Are there deeper subcategories (e.g., by cuisine type or cooking technique)?
- Does `/Arts & Entertainment` appear for the Gordon Ramsay celebrity association?

item.name: 8. Health & Fitness
item.description: Explore the Health and Beauty & Fitness taxonomy branches. Fitness content often appears in both.

request.description:
**Health and fitness content with V2 model.** Tests `/Health` and `/Beauty & Fitness` taxonomy paths.

**What to look for:**
- Does `/Beauty & Fitness` or `/Health` appear? Which scores higher?
- Are there specific fitness subcategories returned?
- Does `/Sports/Sports Coaching & Training` appear?
- Note which top-level branch captures fitness content -- important for ltree mapping.

item.name: 9. YouTube Video Metadata
item.description: Test classification using realistic YouTube video metadata format (title + description + tags). This is the actual format Perspectize will use for auto-classification in Phase 13.

request.description:
**YouTube video metadata classification with V2 model.** Tests the actual input format Perspectize will use in Phase 13 for auto-classification.

The body concatenates: `TITLE + \n\n + DESCRIPTION + \n\n + TAGS` — this gives the classifier maximum context.

**What to look for:**
- Does classification match what you'd manually assign?
- What confidence threshold feels right for primary vs secondary categories?
- Try replacing this content with 2-3 of your own YouTube video titles/descriptions
- Note: API requires at least 20 tokens (words) — metadata format ensures this

**Pro tip:** Duplicate this request and paste your own video metadata to test real content from your YouTube library.
